implementation.improvement: Added an optional verified resynchronization callback. When M156 reports LOSS, the batcher invokes the runtime-owned callback, re-queries occupancy after successful recovery, and resumes only if the new watermarks permit submission.
implementation.fail_closed_behavior: Absent callbacks and callback failures preserve LOSS blocking and EAGAIN behavior. No model output, callback, or userspace result grants kernel authority; the kernel ioctl remains the authorization boundary.
implementation.state_accounting: Tracks resync attempts and failures separately from telemetry-loss observations.
implementation.partial_completion: Existing M157 retained-entry behavior remains unchanged for partial batch completion and retry.

productivity_interpretation.benefit: A runtime with a verified drain/resynchronization procedure can recover automatically from telemetry loss instead of requiring a separate manual acknowledgement path, while still avoiding unsafe submissions when recovery fails.
productivity_interpretation.observed_state: The deterministic test exercised two resynchronization attempts, one successful and one failed, while retaining fail-closed behavior and ending at target batch size one.
productivity_interpretation.raw_throughput_scope: The integrated gate retained the inherited M155 synthetic QEMU accounting benchmark at speedup_x100=114 in this run; M158 does not claim an isolated raw-throughput gain because its change is recovery/control behavior.

build_artifact.kernel_source: M156 kernel image reused; M158 is userspace runtime/test integration.

release_gate.reason: M158 is bounded userspace/QEMU validation. Physical accelerator qualification, independent reproducible production builders, signed artifacts, stable/LTS forward-port qualification, and external security governance remain required.
release_gate.hardware_claim: No physical GPU, NPU, VRAM, IOMMU, DMA, vendor-driver, reset, or fleet qualification is claimed.

known_limitations: The callback is runtime-owned and must implement a real, verified world-state or telemetry drain; the batcher cannot prove semantic resynchronization by itself.
Callback success only permits a re-query; submission remains blocked if the refreshed occupancy/loss state is still unsafe.
The unit test uses an injected ioctl and resync model for deterministic state-machine validation; QEMU validates packaging and integration, not physical accelerator behavior.
No isolated M158 raw-throughput improvement is claimed; the M155 benchmark remains supporting context only.
The kernel remains based on the Linux v7.2-rc7 development line and production release qualification remains incomplete.
